content: 1. Ethinylestradiol can alter hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may necessitate avoiding or substituting the drug. Patients should use additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods and not rely solely on hormonal contraception when taking lesinurad. 2. Ethinylestradiol reduces the efficacy of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Concurrent use of letrozole with estrogens or estrogen-containing products should be avoided or substituted. 3. Ferrous fumarate decreases the absorption and systemic levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or substitute the drug. 4. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor closely for arrhythmias or cardiac events, as its effect on the QT interval is unknown. 5. Lopinavir can significantly alter estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or substitute the drug, and consider non-hormonal contraceptive methods. 6. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control in this scenario. 7. Mavacamten decreases systemic exposure to ethinylestradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or add non-hormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 8. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of metyrapone, potentially leading to subtherapeutic responses. Discontinuation of estrogens, including oral contraceptives, may be advisable prior to and during metyrapone administration. 9. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of minocycline, moxifloxacin, and ofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or substitute the drug. 10. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute the drug. 11. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control in this scenario. 12. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 13. Nelfinavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or substitute the drug, and consider non-hormonal contraceptive methods. 14. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 15. Omaveloxolone reduces the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, including pills, patches, rings, implants, and progestin-only pills, due to weak CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or substitute the drug. 16. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 17. Pentobarbital and phenobarbital decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 18. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 19. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 20. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or substitute the drug. 21. Rifabutin and rifampin decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 22. Ritonavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or substitute the drug, and consider non-hormonal contraceptive methods. 23. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 24. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by receptor binding competition. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients must use additional non-hormonal contraception for seven days after administration. 25. Tipranavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid or substitute the drug, and consider non-hormonal contraceptive methods. 26. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 27. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with hormonal contraceptives. If unavoidable, use additional non-hormonal contraception during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 28. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 29. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance. 30. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 32. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
